title: PRD: Structured emission SLAs, streaming checkpoints, and tool-handoff recovery modes
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: Customers are integrating Redwood streaming responses with downstream tool orchestration systems (webhooks, orchestration engines, internal tool proxies). We need a clear PRD that defines the guarantees we provide for structured output + tool/function calling across normal, degraded, and partial-emission modes. Goal: define deterministic schemas, checkpointing semantics for streaming, error classification and reconciliation strategies, observability signals to anchor SLOs, and test harnesses for acceptance. This PRD captures the acceptance criteria, scope boundaries, and operational runbooks necessary for the feature to be considered shippable.
proposal_summary: Provide a minimal deterministic envelope for streamed structured emissions that supports: (1) deterministic schema frames with versioning; (2) checkpoint markers in the stream so receivers can resume and reconcile partial objects; (3) explicit tool-call lifecycle events (REQUESTED, INVOKED, SUCCEEDED, FAILED) with idempotency keys; (4) a small set of documented error classes and automated fallback policies; (5) telemetry and end-to-end tests that validate correctness under network partitions and retries. Prioritize backward-compatible fallbacks and an opt-in strict-mode for customers requiring stronger guarantees.
scope_changes: Initially scoped to hosted API streaming + SDKs (node/python). Excludes Dedicated private control-plane integration for this tranche; Dedicated will be added in follow-up (linked dependency PM-54890). Adds opt-in strict-mode flag and migration guidance for existing customers sending streamed JSON blobs.
acceptance_criteria: Schema & envelope: All streamed structured responses must be wrapped in a documented envelope with fields: envelope_version (semver string), sequence_token (monotonic integer), frame_type (emission|checkpoint|meta), payload_schema (schema_id), timestamp_iso8601. Tests verify envelope_version and sequence_token monotonicity across network-induced reorderings.

Checkpoint semantics: Checkpoint frames must be emitted at least every N tokens (configurable, default 1024 tokens) and include either a content hash or explicit partial-object path. Consumers can request resume by sending the most recent sequence_token; server must be able to re-emit from the nearest checkpoint within the last 2 checkpoint intervals.

Tool-call lifecycle events: Tool invocations must emit an idempotency_key (UUIDv4), tool_name, request_payload_hash, and lifecycle events: REQUESTED->INVOKED->(SUCCEEDED|FAILED). INVOKED must be emitted before side effects are applied when using Redwood-managed tool gateways. For third-party proxies, we must document eventual-consistency windows.

Error classification and reconciliation: Implement and document three error classes: transient (retryable), repairable (partial output that can be healed via a deterministic retry or manual merge), and terminal (requires user intervention). Acceptance tests must simulate each and assert the client-visible envelope contains error_class and suggested_action fields.

Backwards compatibility & soft-fallback: For clients not opt-in to strict-mode, streams may fall back to best-effort JSON with an initial envelope_version: "0.0.0-legacy". Customers in strict-mode must receive strict schema validation failures (stream aborted with terminal error and telemetry event).

Observability: New telemetry events must include: stream_start, checkpoint_emitted, tool_request_queued, tool_invoked, tool_result_returned, stream_aborted. Each event must carry sequence_token and idempotency_key where applicable. Dashboards for the SLOs below must be provisioned prior to GA.

SLOs & performance: For streaming structured responses in hosted tier: 99th percentile time-to-first-checkpoint <= 200ms for responses <16k tokens; 99th percentile checkpoint emission latency <= 120ms after checkpoint tokenization. Tool-invocation-related tail latency is excluded from stream tokenization SLO by default but must be surfaced separately in the tool dashboard.

E2E test harness: Provide a reproducible harness that runs against staging and simulates: client disconnects, retries with stale sequence_token, duplicated frames, and tool proxy timeouts. Each simulation must include assertions on schema integrity and at-most-once/at-least-once guarantees per tool invocation depending on configuration.

Migration doc & customer guidance: Publish a migration guide with examples for Node/Python SDKs, showing how to resume from checkpoint, how to validate envelope signatures (HMAC for on-prem), and recommended retry windows. The guide must include two worked examples: webhook consumer and orchestration engine adaptor.

Security & privacy: For private deployments, default to encrypting sequence metadata at rest and use KMS-integrated signing of envelope metadata. Security review required and must be completed before GA (see security_review_required=true).
